parties: IndusInd Bank Limited (lender); Lightstorm Telecom Connectivity Pvt. Ltd. (borrower)
headline: Lightstorm secures ₹2,500 crore debt facility from IndusInd Bank for AI-focused terrestrial and subsea fibre network expansion across India and Southeast Asia.
sum: IndusInd Bank extended a ₹2,500 crore debt financing to Lightstorm under a co-borrower structure, fully underwritten for a 10-year tenor. The capital funds the 'AI Superhighway'-a utility-grade fibre network connecting Indian AI hubs (Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad) with hyperscale centres in Singapore and Malaysia via the I-2SEA subsea cable system, in response to accelerating AI compute infrastructure deployment across India.
implication: Co-borrower structure in large infrastructure debt highlights how lenders address multi-entity operational and security frameworks in network-critical projects where segment guarantees and cross-entity recourse are strategically deployed; the fully underwritten 10-year tenor reflects IndusInd's confidence in AI-driven capex-heavy telecom infrastructure, and JSA's documentation of operational security architecture across funded and non-funded facilities is the precedent for multi-tranche infra lending in India's digital backbone build.
detail: Lightstorm, backed by PE firm I Squared Capital and rated CARE AA- (stable), is a network infrastructure company operating >30,000 km terrestrial and 21,000 km subsea fibre globally, connecting >100 data centres. The ₹2,500 crore facility (approx. $260–300 million) is fully underwritten, carries a 10-year tenor, and is structured as a co-borrower arrangement. The proceeds fund (1) a dedicated AI fibre corridor across India's southern corridor linking AI zones in Mumbai, Chennai and Hyderabad, and (2) the India–Southeast Asia (I-2SEA) subsea cable system expansion to Singapore and Malaysia, co-developed with Microsoft, Tata Communications, Singtel, and NEC. The transaction responds to hyperscaler GPU cluster deployment and the emergence of India as a major AI compute market.

framework.ref: Indian Companies Act, 2013, § 2(87) (definition of subsidiary) & § 121 (financial statements of subsidiary companies)
framework.note: Governs structure of Lightstorm entity and consolidated reporting if IndusInd holds significant stakes post-financing.

framework.ref: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Master Direction – Priority Sector Lending (PSL), 2024 or current
framework.note: Determines whether telecom/infrastructure financing qualifies as infrastructure lending and attracts PSL status/exemptions; key for lender capital planning.

framework.ref: RBI Master Direction – Large Exposure Framework, 2024 or current; Basel III Guidelines on Concentration Risk
framework.note: Central to IndusInd's single-obligor large exposure limits (currently capped at 25% of Tier 1 capital) in a ₹2,500 cr facility; requires board approval for limits above 15%.

framework.ref: Indian Telecommunication Act, 1885 & Telecommunication (Broadcasting and Cable) Services Licensing Conditions, as amended
framework.note: Governs right-of-way for deep-trench fibre terrestrial installation and subsea cable landing rights; regulatory approvals for cross-border subsea infrastructure.

framework.ref: Ministry of Communications – Department of Telecom (DoT) Subsea Cable Transmission Standards (2023); International Cable Protection Committee (ICPC) guidelines
framework.note: Regulates subsea cable deployment (I-2SEA), landing permission, and protection zones in Indian waters; cross-border coordination with Singapore, Malaysia.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Regulations, 2015 – Insider Trading (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations, if Lightstorm IPO proceeds (expected mid-2027)
framework.note: Anticipatory: Large debt facility may trigger disclosure obligations post-IPO; material event for public investors.

framework.ref: RBI Master Direction – Know Your Customer (KYC) Norms, 2024 & Anti-Money Laundering (AML) / Combating the Financing of Terrorism (CFT), Schedule 4 to FDI Policy
framework.note: Given I Squared Capital (US-based) backing and cross-border subsea investment, enhanced KYC and foreign investment screening under FIPB/DPIIT regime.

framework.ref: Bharatmala / National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) alignment and Ministry of Communications Digital Communications Backbone fibre policy (2023 onwards)
framework.note: AI Superhighway aligns with government's digital infrastructure agenda; may unlock accelerated environmental/forest clearances and GST concessions.

framework.ref: IndusInd Bank's own Credit Policy & Board-approved Exposure Limits for Infrastructure/Telecom Sector
framework.note: Internal governance: co-borrower structure and security documentation must comply with bank's infrastructure lending framework and stress-test assumptions for AI-driven capex volatility.

conditions: Co-borrower structure (multiple facility tranches: funded and non-funded facilities)
Proceeds for AI Superhighway: terrestrial fibre across southern corridor + I-2SEA subsea cable expansion
Borrower's credit rating: CARE AA- (stable outlook)
Subordination/inter-creditor terms required for co-borrower arrangement
Security framework: pledge of fibre assets, revenue-based repayment covenants linked to AI datacenter utilization (typical for infra debt)
approvals: IndusInd Bank Credit Committee & Board approval for large exposure framework compliance (>15% of Tier 1 capital triggers board sign-off under Basel III)
Department of Telecom (DoT) right-of-way approval for deep-trench installation across southern corridor (Hyderabad–Chennai–Mumbai)
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) / DoT clearance for subsea cable landing at Indian coastal points
Environmental & Forest Clearance for terrestrial fibre trench (State/Central level)
Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) / DPIIT approval (if required) for I Squared Capital's equity backing and cross-border subsea capex
structure.novel: Co-borrower structure for multi-tranche facility across terrestrial and subsea components; operational and security framework linking funded facilities (terrestrial trench, datacenter POPs) with non-funded facilities (subsea cable guarantees, capacity swaps). Represents emerging precedent for infrastructure debt in AI compute backbone where collateral is distributed across geographies (India + Singapore + Malaysia) and asset types (fibre, spectrum, subsea rights-of-way). JSA's documentation framework addresses cross-entity recourse in a consortium project (Microsoft, Tata Communications, Singtel, NEC as I-2SEA co-developers), a novel wrinkle in Indian infrastructure lending.

triggers.law: RBI Master Direction – Large Exposure Framework (2024)
triggers.note: Triggers single-obligor limit review at ₹2,500 cr (likely ~20–22% of IndusInd's Tier 1 capital); board approval mandatory.

triggers.law: Department of Telecom – Right-of-Way Rules, 2016 & amended 2021 (expedited clearance for NIP/digital backbone projects)
triggers.note: AI Superhighway falls under 'critical infrastructure' for AI compute; DoT may accelerate LoA (Letter of Acceptance) given national digital policy alignment.

triggers.law: Telecom (Broadcasting and Cable) Services Licensing Conditions – Subsea Cable Landing Regulations
triggers.note: I-2SEA landing permission in Kerala/Tamil Nadu requires DoT coordination with Singapore & Malaysia governments; cross-border treaty/MOU layer.

triggers.law: SEBI Listing Regulations (anticipatory, for Lightstorm IPO mid-2027)
triggers.note: Post-listing, debt facility becomes material event requiring continuous disclosure; leverage ratio covenants may constrain future equity fundraise.

triggers.law: RBI KYC/AML norms & FIPB foreign investment screening (I Squared Capital, US)
triggers.note: Enhanced KYC required; cross-border capex (subsea) requires foreign exchange outflow RBI approval under Schedule 7, FEMA, 1999.
